Posted April 12, 2001
Special to MarijuanaNews (Thanks to JC for bringing this to my attention.)

Fans of old movies about traveling on trains in Nazi or Communist occupied countries will remember the classic scenes in which the menacing agent with a police dog demands to see the victim’s papers. Or was that the evening news from nark occupied DEAland?

The Albuquerque Journal reports that the local Amtrak office provides the DEA with detailed information on passengers in exchange for 10% of the cash seized from anyone accused of being a " drug courier. "

There is actually a computer linked to Amtrak's Albuquerque ticketing terminal on a desk at the DEA office there. This is supposedly a " one-of-a-kind arrangement. " DEA agents can learn passenger names, points of origin, destinations and where, when and how the tickets were bought. This last point is crucial.

A DEA agent is quoted as saying, " What we looked for are the consistent factors (that) all the seizures we've ever made had in common. And those factors are usually one-way cash tickets bought within three days of the date of departure. "

The assistant director of the local DEA office said he did not know how many arrests had been made or how much money had been seized although both figures were substantial. He claimed that the DEA doesn't limit its train searches to those who buy one-way cash tickets on short notice. He said credit-card purchases made just before departure sometimes raise the suspicion of agents.

Of course, anyone with cash is automatically a " drug courier, " so this can be very profitable. One of the victims was a 26 year-old Vietnamese immigrant who lost $148,000 to this racket. No drugs were found on him and he is suing.

The Albuquerque Journal reported the story as part of an excellent series on cash seizures on the train.
For the full story see
Amtrak Helps DEA Hunt Drug Couriers
and
Immigrant Wants DEA To Give His $148,000 Back

Whatever one may think about marijuana or marijuana prohibition, this story should be frightening to anyone who cares about freedom. Do we really want a police agency reviewing everyone’s travel plans?
